scenario: local STT + cloud cleanup -- the G2a rule
description: The user chose 'Offline' for STT and left a cloud cleanup provider configured. Drift row E2 / D-H10, and grundsatzurteil G2a: no byte leaves the device. PINS: no cleanup call. This is what the desktop HOTKEY has always done and what the React in-app button (D-M20) and Android (D-H10) did not. DOES NOT PIN: what Settings lets the user select (13-3 gates the Android control), only what the runtime does with a stored value.

scenario: local STT + cloud cleanup, no local provider on this platform

scenario: local STT + local cleanup, where local cleanup does NOT exist
description: The same config on a platform with no local LLM. PINS: no cleanup. Before story 13-2 this reached resolve_cleanup_provider's `_ => deepseek` arm, so a fully offline configuration made a cloud call.

scenario: cloud STT + local cleanup, where local cleanup does NOT exist -- drift row D-M21
description: The discriminating row, and the one no pre-13-2 definition got right. One setting ('Local (Offline)' cleanup), three outcomes: on-device on Windows, inert on the Android overlay path, and -- through the Rust in-app button inside TauriActivity, or any non-Windows desktop build -- a plain DeepSeek call, because `"local"` fell through to `_ => cleanup_provider_for("deepseek", …)`. PINS: the answer is NO cleanup. DOES NOT PIN: any user-facing wording; the shipped OfflineRaw outcome is reused and nothing new is shown.

scenario: what each platform reports for local_cleanup_available
description: PINS the platform constants the rows above are parameterised on, so the matrix cannot be read as hypothetical. Rust: `pipeline::local_cleanup_available()` is `cfg!(target_os = "windows")` -- llama-cpp-2 is a Windows-only dependency (project-context: it needs libclang + CMake). Kotlin: `KlarvoOverlayService.LOCAL_CLEANUP_AVAILABLE` is `false` -- Android has no local cleanup and, per G3b, will not get one in this epic. DOES NOT PIN: whether a local provider SHOULD exist on a platform; that is a build decision, not a runtime one.
